A single plastic coffee pod releases 2.3 to 7.9 billion nanoplastic particles into your cup.

Plus 1.2 to 17.8 million microplastic particles. McGill University, 2020.

Aluminium capsules have plastic liners too, just fewer.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/how-to-enjoy-coffee-without-plastic.html

156 over the counter prenatals were tested in 2025. Quantifiable lead in 83 percent of them. Cadmium in 73 percent.

Fifteen percent exceeded the Prop 65 limit of 0.5 micrograms per serving. Prescription prenatals were not immune.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/cleanest-prenatal-vitamins.html

The coating that makes dental floss glide is often PTFE, the same polymer as Teflon.

A 2024 lab study of 39 flosses found PFAS in roughly a third of them. Oral-B Glide tested at 248,900 ppm organic fluorine.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/pfas-free-dental-floss.html

Microplastics in cosmetics hide behind ingredient names, never the word plastic.

Look for polyethylene, polypropylene, PMMA, nylon, PET, acrylates copolymer and polyurethane.

Completely legal, completely unregulated.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/microplastics-in-cosmetics-and-personal-care.html

Clean Label Project testing found 65 percent of chocolate protein powders exceeded California Prop 65 thresholds for heavy metals.

Whey came in at 28 percent, collagen at 26. Chocolate is the flavour carrying the risk.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/cleanest-protein-powder-tested.html

Ceramic coated air fryers are genuinely PTFE and PFAS free, which removes the main chemical concern.

The catch is that ceramic coatings wear faster, so the appliance gets replaced sooner. The tradeoff is durability, not safety.

https://plasticdetox.org/articles/toxic-kitchen-appliances-ranked.html
